title: Introduce CodeLens quickstart: in-editor RAG examples with tool-calling and telemetry bridge
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add CodeLens quickstart: in-editor RAG playground with telemetry bridge and headless smoke harness.
description: Motivation: provide a compact, in-editor quickstart that demonstrates how to wire Redwood RAG flows into a developer workflow inside editors (CodeLens-style inline examples). This quickstart is aimed at developer-experience and docs readers who want a minimal, reproducible example of tool-calling, incremental retrieval, and telemetry capture without standing up a full microservice. What this PR adds: 1) quickstarts/codelens - a lightweight scaffold with an editor sample file that exposes CodeLens anchors which call a local dev shim; 2) telemetry-bridge - a tiny Node process that proxies structured telemetry events from the quickstart to a local file or a configured endpoint (supports stdout, file, or Redwood dev ingest URL); 3) smoke harness - a headless runner for CI that verifies tool-calling sequences and structured output against a golden snapshot; 4) docs page under quickstarts index with runbook and debugging notes; 5) devcontainer and VS Code snippets for immediate onboarding. Implementation notes: the quickstart uses the Redwood JS SDK compatible client (no private APIs), a tiny in-process tool adapter that demonstrates argument serialization and a safe fallback path, and a Handshake step that shows model fallback (small -> medium) for cost-conscious examples. All examples are explicit about batching/kv-cache toggles and include inline guidance for productionization. How to run locally: clone repo, cd quickstarts/codelens, yarn install, start the telemetry bridge (node telemetry-bridge/index.js --mode=file --out=events.json), open the sample in VS Code (devcontainer included) and trigger CodeLens actions or run the headless smoke harness (yarn smoke). Checklist: [x] scaffolds and README, [x] devcontainer and snippets, [x] telemetry bridge, [x] smoke harness + CI job, [x] smoke tests and golden snapshot, [x] docs entry and short-form tutorial. Related: ENG-2104 (devexp initiative), PM-342 (quickstarts roadmap). Notes: kept runtime and SDK usage minimal to avoid coupling to internal toolkits; telemetry bridge intentionally pluggable so platform teams can swap to their ingest. CI: added a lightweight GitHub Actions workflow (quickstart-smoke.yml) that runs smoke harness on Node 18 and reports structured results. Migration/rollback: this is additive and scoped to quickstarts; no runtime or API changes.
